contributions.headingText: Monomorphic epitheliotropic intestinal T-cell lymphoma (MEITL) is a primary intestinal T-cell lymphoma derived from intraepithelial T lymphocytes, characterized by monomorphic cytomorphology and epitheliotropism, typically lacking coeliac disease association.

Most cases present as ulcerative masses in the small intestine or (less commonly) in the colon, duodenum, or stomach, and a small subset of patients may present with multifocal gastrointestinal lesions {23399895; 22641357; 27457239}. In addition to mesenteric lymph nodes, the disease may also disseminate to the lung, liver, and brain.

Most patients present with abdominal pain, gastrointestinal bleeding, obstruction or perforation, diarrhoea, and weight loss {23399895; 22641357; 21921780}. A history of malabsorption or coeliac disease is generally absent.

MEITL has a worldwide distribution. It accounts for many primary intestinal T-cell lymphomas in Asia {21921780; 21753698; 21423155}. It occurs predominantly in adults, with a median patient age in the sixth decade of life and an M:F ratio of about 2:1 {23399895}.

There is clonal rearrangement of the TR genes. Apart from gains of MYC {23399895; 22654438}, also reported are gains at 9q34.3 {26226842; 20399483; 26226842}, 1q32.3, 4p15.1, 5q34, 7q34, 8p11.23, 9q22.31, 9q33.2, and 12p13.31, as well as losses of 7p14.1 and 16q12.1 {26226842; 26854024}. Unlike in type I enteropathy-associated T-cell lymphoma, gains at 1q32.2-q41 and 5q34-q35.5 are uncommon {26854024}.

Activating mutations of STAT5B are noted in cases of both γδ and αβ derivation {26854024; 25586472}. Mutations of JAK3 and GNAI2 may be seen {26854024}. SETD2 is frequently silenced through nonsense mutations, frameshift insertions, and deletions {27600764; 28424246}. EBV is usually negative {23399895; 21921780}.

The tumour is often ulcerated, with transmural invasion. Neoplastic cells are monotonous, small to medium-sized cells with round nuclei, dispersed chromatin, and ample clear cytoplasm. Occasionally neoplastic cells may appear high-grade with a starry-sky appearance or feature greater pleomorphism or more open chromatin. Areas of necrosis and an inflammatory background are uncommon. In the peripheral zone, the tumour invades the adjacent mucosa, which features distorted, broadly expanded villi containing epitheliotropic lymphoma cells. The distant intestinal mucosa features normal architecture and often shows an increase of morphologically bland intraepithelial lymphocytes which may mimic coeliac disease and lymphocytic colitis {23399895; 21921780; 27457239}.

The usual immunophenotype is CD2+, CD3+, CD4−, CD5−, CD7+, CD8+, CD56+ {23399895; 21921780}. Expression of TCRγ or TCRβ may be seen {23399895; 24128129; 23332928}, although a minority is T-cell receptor–silent, and rarely both T-cell receptors are expressed {23399895; 21921780}. One study reported a high incidence of CD8a homodimers {23399895}. The cytotoxic marker TIA1 is expressed in most cases, whereas expression of granzyme B and perforin is less consistent {26226842}. Extensive nuclear expression of MATK is noted {21233830}, and aberrant expression of CD20 is reported in 20% of cases {23399895}. The intraepithelial lymphocytes in the distant zone express CD3, CD8, and TIA1, but they can be positive or negative for CD56 {23399895; 27457239; 21921780} and may represent precursor lesions of MEITL.

Essential: intestine densely infiltrated by monotonous medium-sized T-lineage lymphoid cells, typically lacking necrosis; epithelial invasion commonly present; most common immunophenotype: CD3+, CD5−, CD4−, CD8+, CD56+, cytotoxic marker +.
Lymphoid neoplasms are staged according to the Lugano classification, which has been adopted by the eighth edition of the Union for International Cancer Control (UICC) TNM classification {25113753}.
The clinical outcome for MEITL is poor, with a median survival time of 7 months {23399895}.
